candidate.construction: Both paints use the two admitted fixed-source-ink compounds extracted from the same literal Blode scissors-2 SVG. The outlined and filled part records have identical dimensions and source curves; the emitted SVG serialization differs only in artifact metadata/serialization, and their checker-native rasters are byte-identical.

slimAnchor.note: The packet's filled and outlined scissors-2 references are literally the same SVG bytes and therefore the same proof bytes. This family variant has one broad lower blade and one intrinsically narrow upper blade tip.

curveAndTransformComparison.curveResult: No candidate-authored curve or tip geometry exists. The first compound is the literal scissors-2 main compound under a uniform host transform. Matching source (2,3)->candidate (2,3.25) and source (10,7)->candidate (9.8104,7.1552) gives scale approximately 0.9763 with translation approximately (+0.0474,+0.3211); other reported main-compound coordinates agree to the four-decimal serialization precision.
curveAndTransformComparison.placementResult: The source scissors-2 SVG already separates its lower blade as a second compound. The candidate places the extracted main compound at top-left 2,3 and the extracted lower-blade compound at top-left 14.5,12.5, then center+fit uniformly reduce the assembled drawing. Thus fit reduces both blade weights together; it does not selectively thin the upper tip. Splitting/replacing the second compound only changes its relative placement by the quantized top-left placement before the shared fit.

nativeRasterComparison.method: Rendered the immutable literal scissors-2 source SVG and immutable candidate SVG through the workspace Sharp renderer at 16 and 32 pixels, flattened black on white, then compared grayscale bytes. This is a diagnostic rerender, not replacement canonical evidence.
nativeRasterComparison.interpretation: The small global fit/placement change makes the whole candidate slightly lighter than the literal source. In matched 16px right-side sample windows, source-to-candidate ink decreased for both upper and lower blade regions (upper -164 gray-ink units; lower -132). The effect is not confined to the upper tip.

lobeVariant.construction: separate lobe/ring and heavier blade-body construction

slimVariant.construction: asymmetric slim upper blade and broad lower wedge in one literal source silhouette

variantSeparation.decision: Using scissors-1/50903 tip weight as a required correction would hybridize two admitted house variants. It is valid only as an explicit choice to switch variants, not evidence that this scissors-2 reconstruction introduced a tip-specific defect.

conclusion.qualification: The upper-tip lightness is visible and slightly amplified by the candidate's approximately 2.37% uniform fit reduction, but its asymmetric tip topology is inherited exactly from the admitted scissors-2 house source. The measurable candidate-specific change is the small uniform scale plus quantized second-compound placement, affecting both tips and rings. The A146 proposed upper-only thickening is therefore a cross-variant style preference, not an objective repair of candidate-authored geometry.
